about.title: Fremont Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product rarely announces itself. In Fremont, it might be a space heater in a Warm Springs apartment, a power tool in a Niles garage, or a tire that lets go on I-880 during the Friday evening rush. Whatever the object, the legal question is the same: was it defective in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and did that defect cause your injury? Under California law, that is usually enough. You generally do not have to prove the company was careless. That is what strict liability means, and it matters for people in Alameda County who were simply using an item the way it was meant to be used. Responsibility can also reach beyond the manufacturer to the distributor and the store that sold it. The single most useful thing you can do is keep the product, its packaging, and any receipts exactly as they are. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that matches Fremont residents with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My car part failed on I-680 in Fremont and caused a crash. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Fremont recorded 799 injury collisions in 2025, and while most involve driver error, some trace back to a defective component such as a brake, tire, or airbag. If a part failed, the manufacturer or seller may be liable under strict liability in addition to any driver. An attorney can help sort out which claims apply and make sure the vehicle and part are preserved.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it, and do not repair, clean, or throw it away. The product itself is often the most important evidence, along with its packaging, manual, and proof of purchase. Take photos of the item and your injuries, and write down where and when you bought it. An attorney can arrange for proper storage and testing.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company knew the product was unsafe?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability often runs on strict liability, so the focus is on whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and whether that defect caused your injury. You generally do not need to show the company acted carelessly. That said, every case has its own facts, which is why speaking with an attorney matters.
